For each distribution, calculate the sum of Si for each customer and determine the number of distinct prime factors in each sum. Track the maximum revenue obtained across all distributions.

Utilize dynamic programming to optimize the solution. Define a DP state as the maximum revenue achievable using a subset of the data pieces. Transition between states by considering whether to include the current data piece in the current customer's group or start a new group for this piece. This approach avoids redundant calculations and efficiently explores all possible distributions.

Implement a greedy algorithm that prioritizes grouping data pieces with similar prime factor counts together. Start by calculating the number of distinct prime factors for each Si. Group the data pieces based on these counts, aiming to minimize the number of distinct prime factors in each group. This heuristic may not always yield the optimal solution but can provide a good approximation in practice.
